# Elliptic &amp; Parabolic Functions

![Elliptic &amp; Parabolic Functions function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/elliptic-parabolic-functions/00_Repertoire%20Elliptic%20%26%20Parabolic%20functions.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Jacobi cn, dn, sn and amplitude phi; normalized parabolic cylinder Dv(x). ni_documented_real_v1 evaluates x through abs; standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. k is the parameter m; v is a real order. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured.

## Browse this palette

This entry opens a palette folder; it is not an executable dataflow function.

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Jacobi Elliptic](../../math/special/elliptic_parabolic_functions/jacobi_elliptic.md) | Evaluates Jacobi cn, dn, sn and continuous amplitude phi for real x and parameter m=k (not k squared and not the modulus). Domain 0&lt;=k&lt;=1. phi is in radians and retains its periods: phi(u+2K)=phi(u)+pi. At k=0: cos(u),1,sin(u),u; at k=1: sech(u),sech(u),tanh(u),2 atan(tanh(u/2)). At x=1,k=.25: cn=.568568998095171, dn=.911492005669132, sn=.822635578129862, phi=.966031052636614. Both inputs f64 required without defaults. ni_documented_real_v1 uses u=abs(x), never abs(k), abs(v) or abs(result); standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured. |
| [Parabolic Cylinder](../../math/special/elliptic_parabolic_functions/parabolic_cylinder.md) | Evaluates the normalized parabolic cylinder function Dv(x), the Weber solution with Dv(z)~z^v exp(-z*z/4) at positive infinity. v is a real order: negative and fractional values are accepted without rounding or abs(v). Exactly one output Dv(x), no derivative. D0(1)=D1(1)=.778800783071405; D2(0)=-1 and D2(1)=0; D0.5(1)=.842203244069840. Finite x and v define a real function; machine limits are diagnosed separately. Both inputs f64 required without defaults. ni_documented_real_v1 uses u=abs(x), never abs(k), abs(v) or abs(result); standard_real_v1 keeps signed x. NI-G documentation; NI/NXG runtime parity unmeasured. |
